identity.title: Reinforcement Learning Under Latent Dynamics: Toward Statistical and Algorithmic Modularity

problem.claim: Characterize reinforcement learning under general latent dynamics from statistical and algorithmic perspectives.

gap.claim: Beyond restrictive cases such as tabular latent dynamics, the statistical requirements and algorithmic principles remain poorly understood.

contributions.claim: Shows that most well-studied function-approximation settings become intractable when combined with rich observations, and identifies latent pushforward coverability as a general condition for statistical tractability.
Develops provably efficient observable-to-latent reductions for hindsight observations and self-predictive latent-model estimation settings.
Positions the results as an initial step toward a unified statistical and algorithmic theory of reinforcement learning under latent dynamics.

stated_novelty.claim: The paper presents a unified statistical and algorithmic treatment of reinforcement learning under general latent dynamics, including latent pushforward coverability and observable-to-latent reductions.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report a negative result: most established function-approximation settings become intractable after composition with rich observations.
The authors report a positive result identifying latent pushforward coverability as a condition enabling statistical tractability.
The authors report provable efficiency of observable-to-latent reductions in the hindsight-observation and self-predictive-model settings.

narrative_sequence.summary: Real-world reinforcement-learning environments may expose complex, high-dimensional observations despite comparatively simple latent dynamics.
The statistical requirements and algorithmic principles for general latent dynamics are described as poorly understood beyond tabular settings.
The paper reports both broad intractability under rich observations and a tractability condition, latent pushforward coverability.
It develops observable-to-latent reductions under hindsight observations and self-predictive latent-model estimation.
The combined results are presented as a first step toward a unified theory.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs a negative statistical result with a positive condition for tractability, then links both to concrete reduction settings.

lessons.interpretation: This pairing makes the boundary of feasibility more informative than presenting only an algorithm or only a hardness result.
lessons.application: Frame a theory paper around an explicit obstruction followed by a condition or structural assumption that restores tractability, and connect the assumption to an implementable reduction.
lessons.exception: Avoid this framing when the work has no meaningful negative result or when the proposed condition is not formally tied to the method's operating regime.

unknowns: The abstract does not define latent pushforward coverability or specify the exact function classes and hardness notion behind “most” and “intractable.”
The efficiency guarantees, assumptions, sample complexities, and algorithmic details of the reductions are unspecified.
No empirical evaluation or experimental conditions are reported in the supplied units.
